newsitem.title: USA: State security regulators okay adviser scheme.
newsitem.headline: State security regulators okay adviser scheme.

text.p: A group of state securities regulators said Monday they approved a new plan to regulate small investment advisers while leaving federal regulators to oversee larger ones.

"We are committed to having this plan implemented by July 8th when these financial professionals become our exclusive regulatory charge," said Mark Griffin, North American Securities Administrators Association Inc. (NASAA) president.
The new initiative, approved Sunday, is geared toward the growing number of consumers who use small investment advisers and financial planners, NASAA said.
The new plan will give states primary regulatory responsibility for some 19,000 of the 25,000 investment advisers and financial planners nationwide.
The agreement calls for, among other things, yearly training of new regulatory personnel, and sharing information and communication support among securities regulators.
The accord, approved at NASAA's spring conference here, also calls for working groups to develop uniform financial and record keeping regulations for state-registered advisers.
According to the pact, NASAA will develop an exam for its members testing knowledge of subject matter and competency of state-registered investment adviser representatives.

The plan, slated to become effective in July, is a provision of the National Securities Markets Improvement Act, sweeping securities reform legistation designed to do away with overlapping state and federal regulations of advisers.
The Securities and Exchange Commission retained oversight of investment advisers with more than $25 million in assets under management.
